q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: Dogs are always loyal ____ their master.
explanation:
'Loyal' always takes 'to': loyal to someone/something (loyal to one's country, loyal to a friend).
Memory hook: you are loyal TO whom you are devoted TO.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: She is not fond ____ milk.
explanation:
'Fond' takes 'of': fond of music, fond of children. 'Off' is a different word (away from).
Memory hook: fond OF = full OF liking.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: I will wait ____ the bus stop.
explanation:
Use 'at' for a specific point/location such as a stop, gate or corner: at the bus stop, at the door.
Memory hook: AT = a point on the map; IN = inside an enclosed space.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: I have lived here ____ twenty years.
explanation:
'For' + a period of time (for twenty years, for two hours); 'since' + a point of time (since 2005, since Monday).
Memory hook: FOR a length, SINCE a starting point.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: He is afraid ____ the dark.
explanation:
'Afraid' takes 'of': afraid of the dark, afraid of dogs. ('Afraid for' means worried about someone's safety.)
Memory hook: scared OF = afraid OF.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: They turned ____ my offer.
explanation:
'Turn down' = reject/refuse (an offer, a proposal). 'Turn off' = switch off; 'turn away' = refuse entry or look away.
Memory hook: thumbs DOWN to an offer = turn it DOWN.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: She was prepared ____ the worst.
explanation:
'Prepared for' + noun (prepared for the exam, prepared for the worst); 'prepared to' + verb (prepared to wait).
Memory hook: ready FOR a thing, ready TO do.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: They walked slowly ____ the woods.
explanation:
'Through' = from one side to the other of an enclosed area: walk through the woods/tunnel/crowd.
Memory hook: THROUGH = in one side, out the other.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: She congratulated me ____ my success.
explanation:
'Congratulate someone on something' is the standard usage: congratulated him on his promotion.
Memory hook: congratulate ON = the praise lands ON your achievement.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: She refrained ____ making any comment.
explanation:
'Refrain from' + -ing = hold oneself back from doing: refrain from smoking.
Memory hook: refrain FROM = keep away FROM (like abstain from, desist from).

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: She drove alone ____ the movies.
explanation:
'To' marks the destination of movement: drove to the movies, went to school.
Memory hook: motion TOwards a destination = TO.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: He walked ____ me angrily.
explanation:
'Towards' = in the direction of; with a verb of motion (walked) it shows direction: he walked towards me.
Memory hook: TOWARDS = heading in someone's direction.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: He was not accustomed ____ working alone.
explanation:
'Accustomed to' + noun/-ing (the 'to' is a preposition, so -ing follows): accustomed to working, used to living.
Memory hook: accustomed TO = used TO.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: She is capable ____ hurting me.
explanation:
'Capable of' + noun/-ing: capable of hurting, capable of great work. (Compare: able TO + verb.)
Memory hook: capable OF, able TO.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: We are familiar ____ the situation.
explanation:
A person is 'familiar with' something (knows it well); something is 'familiar to' a person. 'We are familiar with the situation.'
Memory hook: I am familiar WITH it; it is familiar TO me.

q: Find the part of the sentence that has an error ((A), (B) or (C)); mark (D) if there is no error: The river (A) / has overflown (B) / its banks. (C) / No error (D)
explanation:
'Overflow' is a regular verb: overflow - overflowed - overflowed. 'Overflown' is the past participle of 'overfly' (to fly over). Correct: 'The river has overflowed its banks.'
Memory hook: rivers overflow(ED), planes overfl(OWN).

q: Find the part of the sentence that has an error ((A), (B) or (C)); mark (D) if there is no error: The scientists (A) / could not hardly (B) / complete all the experiments. (C) / No error (D)
explanation:
'Hardly' is already negative; 'not hardly' is a double negative. Correct: 'could hardly complete'.
Memory hook: hardly, scarcely, barely = built-in NOT - never add another.

q: Find the part of the sentence that has an error ((A), (B) or (C)); mark (D) if there is no error: Martin Luther King was one of the leaders (A) / who (B) / has followed Mahatma Gandhi. (C) / No error (D)
options: Martin Luther King was one of the leaders
explanation:
In 'one of the + plural noun + who', the relative clause refers to the plural noun (leaders), and the sentence is in the past. So 'has followed' is wrong; use 'followed' (or 'have followed').
Memory hook: 'one of the leaders WHO...' - WHO = the leaders (plural).

q: Find the part of the sentence that has an error ((A), (B) or (C)); mark (D) if there is no error: Never once (A) / I have seen (B) / such a beautiful sight. (C) / No error (D)
explanation:
When a negative adverb (never, seldom, hardly, not once) begins a sentence, subject and auxiliary are inverted: 'Never once have I seen such a beautiful sight.'
Memory hook: NEGATIVE first -> QUESTION word order.

q: Find the part of the sentence that has an error ((A), (B) or (C)); mark (D) if there is no error: I was surprised (A) / when I heard that (B) / she was won the match. (C) / No error (D)
explanation:
'She was won the match' mixes passive 'was' with an active meaning. She did the winning, before the hearing, so use past perfect: 'she had won the match'.
Memory hook: earlier of two past actions -> HAD + V3.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom/phrase: To eat humble pie
explanation:
'Eat humble pie' = admit a mistake and apologise humbly.
Memory hook: HUMBLE pie - you swallow your pride and say sorry.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom/phrase: Left no stone unturned
explanation:
'Leave no stone unturned' = try every possible means; make every effort.
Memory hook: looking under EVERY stone = trying everything.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom/phrase: In cold blood
explanation:
'In cold blood' = deliberately and without pity; ruthlessly (murdered in cold blood).
Memory hook: COLD blood = no warm feelings, no mercy.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom/phrase: Crocodile tears
explanation:
'Crocodile tears' = false, insincere show of sorrow (from the myth that crocodiles weep while eating prey).
Memory hook: the crocodile cries while it eats you - fake grief.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom/phrase: To leave someone in the lurch
explanation:
'Leave someone in the lurch' = abandon someone when they are in difficulty and need help.
Memory hook: LURCH = a sudden stagger - you walk away just as they stumble.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom/phrase: A black sheep
explanation:
'Black sheep' = a member of a family/group regarded as a disgrace.
Memory hook: the one dark sheep in a white flock - the family's odd, shameful one.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom/phrase: At sixes and sevens
explanation:
'At sixes and sevens' = in confusion or disorder.
Memory hook: numbers scattered like dice - things all over the place.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom/phrase: Cut short
explanation:
'Cut short' = bring to an end early; interrupt (He cut me short = he interrupted me; the trip was cut short).
Memory hook: cut the talk SHORT = stop it before it's finished.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom/phrase: Pull a long face
explanation:
'Pull (or wear) a long face' = look sad, disappointed or gloomy.
Memory hook: a drooping, LONG face = a sad face.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom/phrase: To drive home
options: to return to place of rest
explanation:
'Drive (a point) home' = make something clearly understood; emphasise it forcefully.
Memory hook: hammer a nail HOME - push the point all the way in.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word (shown in capitals): Both parties signed an ACCORD last week in Geneva.
explanation:
'Accord' = an official agreement or harmony. Opposite: disagreement. Rapport, consensus and conformity are all close to agreement.
Memory hook: 'in accord' = in agreement; 'discord' is its opposite.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word (shown in capitals): I do not want to DIVULGE my plan.
explanation:
'Divulge' = make known (secret information). Opposite: conceal (hide). Disclose, leak and reveal are synonyms.
Memory hook: DIVULGE = DIVe out and spill; CONCEAL = keep sealed.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word (shown in capitals): The ARID soil is unsuitable for agriculture.
explanation:
'Arid' = very dry; producing little vegetation. Opposite: fertile. Dry, parched and barren are synonyms.
Memory hook: ARID = desert-like (Arabian desert); FERTILE = farm-friendly.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word (shown in capitals): They were admiring the LUSTRE of the new table.
explanation:
'Lustre' = gentle shine or gloss. Opposite: dullness. Sheen is a synonym.
Memory hook: LUSTRE ~ ILLUSTRIOUS ~ shining; dull = no shine.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word (shown in capitals): She seemed INVINCIBLE.
explanation:
'Invincible' = too strong to be defeated. Opposite: vulnerable (easily hurt or attacked).
Memory hook: in-VINC-ible = cannot be VANQuished; VULNERable = can be wounded (Latin vulnus = wound).

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Cherish
explanation:
'Cherish' = hold dear, protect lovingly = treasure. The others mean ignore or give up.
Memory hook: CHERISH = keep like a CHERished treasure.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Capitulate
explanation:
'Capitulate' = surrender, give in = concede. Resist and defy are opposites.
Memory hook: capitulate - the city's CAPITAL falls, it gives up.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Disdain
explanation:
'Disdain' = the feeling that someone/something is unworthy = contempt, scorn. Esteem and admiration are opposites.
Memory hook: DIS-dain = DIS-respect.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Obsolete
explanation:
'Obsolete' = no longer in use; out of date = outdated. Contemporary (modern) is the opposite.
Memory hook: typewriters are OBSOLETE - OLD and OUT.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Annexure
explanation:
'Annexure' = something added or attached, e.g. an appendix to a document = attachment.
Memory hook: ANNEX = an added wing of a building; annexure = an attached document.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate word(s): The Principal ____ permission to the students to celebrate.
explanation:
'Grant permission' is the fixed collocation. 'Allowed permission' is redundant; prizes are 'awarded'.
Memory hook: authorities GRANT permission, a visa, a request.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate word(s): Voters are beginning to take ____ him as a serious candidate.
explanation:
The phrase is 'take notice of' = pay attention to.
Memory hook: take notice OF, take care OF, take note OF.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate word(s): If I had helped him, he ____.
explanation:
Third conditional (unreal past): If + had + V3, ... would have + V3. So: 'If I had helped him, he would not have drowned.'
Memory hook: HAD in the if-clause -> WOULD HAVE in the result.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate word(s): When will you hand ____ your assignment?
explanation:
'Hand in' = submit (work, a form, an assignment). 'Hand back' = return; 'hand down' = pass to the next generation.
Memory hook: hand IN = put it IN the teacher's tray.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate word(s): The hotel was not too expensive, ____.
explanation:
Question tags: negative statement -> positive tag, using the same auxiliary and tense. 'was not' -> 'was it?'
Memory hook: tags flip polarity: NOT ... -> positive tag.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate word(s): She remained a/an ____ all her life.
explanation:
A woman who never marries is traditionally a 'spinster' (a noun, fitting 'a/an ___'). 'Bachelor' is for a man; 'unmarried' and 'single' are adjectives and would not follow 'a/an' without a noun.
Memory hook: SPINster - she spun wool at home; BACHELOR - he.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate word(s): There is something strange ____ him.
explanation:
'Something strange/odd/special about someone' is the idiomatic use of 'about' = concerning, in the nature of.
Memory hook: there's something ABOUT him.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate word(s): He went there ____.
explanation:
The standard idiom is 'on foot' (but 'by car, by bus, by train'). 'Walking on foot' is redundant.
Memory hook: ON foot, ON horseback; BY every vehicle.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate word(s): We must eliminate the ____ the rich and the poor.
explanation:
A disparity (gap/inequality) exists 'between' two things: disparity between the rich and the poor.
Memory hook: a GAP is always BETWEEN two sides.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate word(s): The actual ____ of sleep you need depends on your age.
explanation:
'Amount' is used with uncountable nouns (sleep, water, money); 'number' with countable nouns (hours, people). Sleep is uncountable.
Memory hook: AMOUNT of stuff you can't count; NUMBER of things you can.

q: Where does Meghalaya have its railhead?
explanation:
Mendipathar in North Garo Hills has Meghalaya's first and only railway station, on the Dudhnoi-Mendipathar line (inaugurated 30 November 2014). As of the 2025 exam, the planned Tetelia-Byrnihat line to Byrnihat (Ri-Bhoi) had not opened, having been held up for years by local opposition.
Memory hook: Meghalaya's first train arrived in the Garo hills (Mendipathar), not in Khasi-Jaintia.
note: As of Sep 2026: Mendipathar is still Meghalaya's only railway station; the Tetelia-Byrnihat line is still a planned/under-construction project and has not opened.

q: Which input device converts the motion by a user into cursor movement on the monitor screen?
explanation:
The device that turns hand motion into cursor movement is the mouse (or trackball/touchpad). Mouse is not among the options. Of the four, only the keyboard is an input device, and its arrow keys move the cursor, so the key accepts Keyboard.
Memory hook: MOUSE = Motion Of User Steers Everything on screen.
note: The options look copied from Q75 (embedded computers). The textbook answer, mouse, is not among them. The official key gives (C) Keyboard as the only input device listed.

q: Who is known as the 'father of humanism'?
explanation:
Francesco Petrarch (1304-1374), the Italian poet-scholar, revived the study of classical Latin texts. That revival started Renaissance humanism, so he is called the 'Father of Humanism'.
Memory hook: PETRarch -> PETs of the Renaissance were the old Greek and Roman classics.

q: In which year did the First World War begin?
explanation:
World War I began in July 1914, after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo. It ended in November 1918. World War II began in 1939.
Memory hook: WWI = 1914-18; WWII = 1939-45.

q: Hongkong is located at the mouth of which river?
explanation:
Hong Kong (with Macau and Guangzhou) sits on the Pearl River Delta in southern China, where the Pearl (Zhujiang) River meets the South China Sea. Shanghai is on the Yangtze mouth.
Memory hook: Hong Kong is the 'Pearl of the Orient' on the Pearl River.

q: In which year, did the UNESCO add the Nokrek National Park to its list of Biosphere Reserve?
explanation:
Nokrek Biosphere Reserve (West Garo Hills) joined UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves (Man and the Biosphere programme) in May 2009. Nokrek is the highest peak of the Garo Hills and is known for wild citrus (Citrus indica).
Memory hook: Nokrek went global in 2009, the year of the wild orange.

q: What was the name of the Satellite that the Soviet Union launched into space on 4th October, 1957?
explanation:
Sputnik 1, launched by the USSR on 4 October 1957, was the first artificial satellite and started the Space Age. Laika was the dog aboard Sputnik 2 (November 1957). Voyager was a later US probe.
Memory hook: Sputnik = 'fellow traveller' in Russian, the first companion of Earth.

q: During the Partition of India, about one-third of Kashmir became the part of which country?
explanation:
After the 1947-48 war, roughly one-third of the former princely state of Jammu & Kashmir (now called Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, i.e. 'Azad Kashmir' + Gilgit-Baltistan) came under Pakistan's control. Bangladesh did not exist until 1971.
Memory hook: 1947 Partition = India and Pakistan only; Bangladesh came later.

q: Who invented the printing press with movable type?
explanation:
Johannes Gutenberg of Mainz, Germany built the movable-type printing press around 1440. It printed the Gutenberg Bible (c. 1455). Boyle was a chemist; da Gama and Magellan were explorers.
Memory hook: GUTENberg printed the GOOD book (the Bible).

q: Who was India's first sportsperson to receive the Padma Vibhushan Award?
explanation:
Chess Grandmaster Viswanathan Anand is popularly cited as the first sportsperson to receive the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award. The official MHA Padma Awards directory lists him in the 2008 Padma Vibhushan list (presented 10 May 2008), the same list that included Sachin Tendulkar; Anand is named first there. Mary Kom got it in 2020, and Neeraj Chopra has never received it.
Memory hook: Anand made the first 'move' (chess) to Padma Vibhushan.
note: Many GK books say Anand got the award in 2007. The official MHA directory puts both Anand and Sachin Tendulkar in the 2008 list, so 'first' really means 'first-named in the first list with sportspersons'. The official key gives (C) Anand.

q: Who is the present Speaker of the Meghalaya Legislative Assembly?
explanation:
Thomas A. Sangma (NPP, North Tura) was elected Speaker of the 11th Meghalaya Legislative Assembly on 9 March 2023 and was Speaker at the April 2025 exam. Timothy D. Shira was Deputy Speaker at that time. Dr. Donkupar Roy (Speaker 2018-2023) died in 2023.
Memory hook: Thomas from Tura holds the Speaker's chair.
note: As of Sep 2026: Thomas A. Sangma is still Speaker. The Deputy Speaker is now Limison D. Sangma (NPP, since 12 September 2025); Timothy D. Shira became Fisheries Minister in September 2025.

q: Mesopotamia is located between which two rivers?
explanation:
Mesopotamia (Greek: 'land between the rivers') is the land between the Tigris and Euphrates, mostly in present-day Iraq. It was the cradle of the Sumerian civilisation. The Nile is in Egypt.
Memory hook: meso = middle, potamos = river; the two rivers are 'T and E'.

q: Where was Napoleon born?
explanation:
Napoleon Bonaparte was born in 1769 in Ajaccio, on the island of Corsica. France had acquired Corsica from Genoa only a year earlier. Elba was where he was first exiled (1814), and St Helena was where he died.
Memory hook: Born on Corsica, exiled to Elba, died on St Helena (C-E-S).

q: What was the first domesticated animal?
explanation:
The dog, domesticated from the grey wolf by hunter-gatherers more than 15,000 years ago, was the first domesticated animal. That was well before sheep, goats and cattle, which came with farming about 10,000 years ago.
Memory hook: man's best friend was also man's first friend.

q: Which King brought Buddhism to Kashmir?
explanation:
Emperor Ashoka (Maurya, 3rd century BCE) spread Buddhism across his empire, including Kashmir. Tradition credits him with founding Srinagari and sending missionaries such as Majjhantika there. Babur was a Mughal, Sri Gupta founded the Gupta dynasty, and Abdagases was an Indo-Parthian king.
Memory hook: Ashoka = the great Buddhist missionary emperor.

q: Which is the largest national cave in South Asia?
explanation:
Krem Liat Prah in the Jaintia Hills, Meghalaya, is the longest natural cave in South Asia (about 30+ km, part of the Liat Prah-Umim-Labit system). Langun-Gobingob is in the Philippines and Boybuloq is in Uzbekistan.
Memory hook: 'Krem' = cave in Khasi; Meghalaya's caves lead South Asia.
note: 'national cave' is a misprint for 'natural cave'. Krem Liat Prah is usually described as the longest natural cave in the Indian subcontinent.

q: What is the term used when a company receives control over the entire market?
explanation:
A monopoly is a market with a single seller who controls the entire supply. An oligopoly has a few sellers, and perfect competition has many.
Memory hook: mono = one seller; oligo = few; perfect = many.

q: What was the first spaceflight to orbit the Moon?
explanation:
Apollo 8 (December 1968; Borman, Lovell, Anders) was the first crewed spacecraft to orbit the Moon; it took the 'Earthrise' photo. Apollo 11 (1969) was the first to land. Gemini and Mercury flights stayed in Earth orbit.
Memory hook: 8 circled first, 11 landed.

q: Which mountain range has historically been the natural dividing line between Northern and Southern India?
explanation:
The Vindhya Range (with the Satpura and the Narmada valley) runs across central India. It has traditionally divided North India (Aryavarta) from the Deccan / South India (Dakshinapatha).
Memory hook: Vindhya = the 'waist-belt' of India.

q: Who founded the Non-Cooperation Movement against the British rule in India?
explanation:
Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920 (approved at the Calcutta special session and at Nagpur). It was withdrawn in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident. Annie Besant led the Home Rule League, and W.C. Banerjee was the first INC president.
Memory hook: NCM 1920 -> Chauri Chaura 1922 -> Gandhi calls it off.

q: When did Meghalaya become an Autonomous State within Assam?
explanation:
Meghalaya became an autonomous state within Assam on 2 April 1970, under the Assam Reorganisation (Meghalaya) Act, 1969. It became a full-fledged state on 21 January 1972.
Memory hook: 2-4-70 autonomous, 21-1-72 full state.

q: What is the capital city of Tasmania?
explanation:
Hobart is the capital of Tasmania, Australia's island state. Sydney is the capital of New South Wales, Perth of Western Australia, and Darwin of the Northern Territory.
Memory hook: Tasmania's Hobart = 'Harbour-Bart' on the Derwent estuary.

q: Which is sometimes known as the 'hidden' tax?
explanation:
Economists commonly call inflation the 'hidden tax' because it quietly erodes purchasing power without any legislation. Indirect taxes built into the price of goods, such as excise duty, are also described as hidden because the buyer does not see them separately. Excise is the closest option.
Memory hook: you pay it without seeing it -> hidden.
note: Official key: full marks to all (NOTA) - correct answer not among options; actual fact: inflation is the term usually called the 'hidden tax'. Option (C) Excise tax is given here only as the closest option.

q: According to the SIPRI report, which country became the largest arms importer in the world during 2020-2024?
explanation:
SIPRI's 'Trends in International Arms Transfers, 2024' (March 2025) ranked Ukraine the world's largest arms importer for 2020-24, driven by the war with Russia. India was second.
Memory hook: war-time Ukraine overtook India at the top.
note: As of Sep 2026: SIPRI's next report (March 2026, covering 2021-25) again ranks Ukraine first (9.7% of global arms imports) and India second.

q: Which of the following is not an example of an embedded computer?
explanation:
An embedded computer is a microprocessor system built inside a device to do one dedicated job, e.g. DVD players, digital watches, GPS units, washing machines. A keyboard is treated as an input peripheral of a general-purpose computer, not an embedded computer.
Memory hook: embedded = computer hidden INSIDE an appliance; a keyboard just feeds a computer.

q: Which enlightenment thinker is known for the concept of 'separation of powers'?
explanation:
Montesquieu set out the separation of powers (legislature, executive, judiciary) in 'The Spirit of the Laws' (1748). Hobbes wrote 'Leviathan', Adam Smith wrote 'The Wealth of Nations', and Voltaire championed free speech.
Memory hook: MONTesquieu split power into three MOUNTains.

q: The Industrial Revolution began in which country?
explanation:
The Industrial Revolution began in England (Great Britain) around 1760. It was driven by textile machinery, coal and James Watt's improved steam engine.
Memory hook: steam, spinning jenny and coal -> Britain first.

q: In which year was the World Health Organization founded?
explanation:
WHO was established on 7 April 1948, headquartered in Geneva. 7 April is celebrated as World Health Day.
Memory hook: World Health Day 7 April = WHO's birthday (1948).

q: Longitude lines
options: run east and west of Equator
run north and south of Prime Meridian
explanation:
Longitudes (meridians) are half-circles that run from the North Pole to the South Pole, so all of them meet at the poles. They are measured 0-180 degrees east or west of the Prime Meridian. Latitudes run parallel to the Equator and go up to 90 degrees.
Memory hook: LONGitudes are LONG lines pole-to-pole; latitudes are flat like ladder rungs.

q: Who is the first Indian Boxer to win an Olympic medal?
explanation:
Vijender Singh won bronze (middleweight) at the Beijing 2008 Olympics, India's first Olympic boxing medal. Mary Kom won bronze in 2012 and Lovlina Borgohain won bronze in 2020 (Tokyo).
Memory hook: 2008 Vijender, 2012 Mary, 2020 Lovlina.

q: When was the Meghalaya High Court established?
explanation:
The High Court of Meghalaya was established on 23 March 2013, along with the High Courts of Manipur and Tripura, by separating them from the Gauhati High Court.
Memory hook: 2013 - three NE states got their own High Courts together.

q: What is the Monarch of Egypt called?
explanation:
The rulers of ancient Egypt were called Pharaohs (from 'per-aa', the 'great house'). Examples: Tutankhamun, Ramses II.
Memory hook: Pharaoh -> Pyramids.
note: Refers to ancient Egypt. Modern Egypt is a republic and has no monarch; its last king, Fuad II, was deposed in 1953.

q: Name the organ responsible for blood purification in human body.
explanation:
The kidneys filter the blood through about a million nephrons each. They remove urea and excess salts and water as urine. The liver detoxifies chemicals, but the standard answer for blood filtration/purification is the kidney.
Memory hook: kidney = the body's water filter (dialysis replaces it).

q: Who has the power to declare a National Emergency in India?
options: The Governor of the respective State
explanation:
Under Article 352, the President declares a National Emergency, on the written advice of the Union Cabinet (44th Amendment, 1978), on grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion.
Memory hook: 352 - President proclaims, Cabinet advises in writing.

q: When is National Science Day observed?
explanation:
National Science Day is observed on 28 February. It marks C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect (28 February 1928), for which he won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Memory hook: 28-2-28 -> Raman Effect.

q: Wings of Fire is the autobiography of which Indian?
options: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
explanation:
'Wings of Fire' (1999, with Arun Tiwari) is the autobiography of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, the 'Missile Man' and 11th President of India.
Memory hook: missiles have fiery wings -> Missile Man's story.

q: Who discovered the law of gravity?
explanation:
Sir Isaac Newton formulated the law of universal gravitation in 'Principia' (1687); the famous story is the falling apple. Einstein later gave General Relativity (1915), and Darwin gave the theory of evolution.
Memory hook: Newton + apple = gravity.

q: The Right to Information (RTI) Act was enacted in which year?
explanation:
The Right to Information Act was passed in 2005 (assent 15 June 2005; fully in force 12 October 2005). It replaced the Freedom of Information Act, 2002.
Memory hook: RTI = 2005; 30 days to reply.

q: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states 'equality of opportunity in public employment'?
explanation:
Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment. Article 14 gives equality before law, Article 18 abolishes titles, and Article 12 defines 'State'.
Memory hook: 16 -> sixteen-year-olds dream of jobs; Art. 16 = jobs.

q: The name 'Meghalaya' was coined by
explanation:
The name 'Meghalaya' ('abode of clouds', Sanskrit) was coined by the geographer Prof. Shiba Prasad (S.P.) Chatterjee of Calcutta University.
Memory hook: S.P. Chatterjee - a geographer named the 'cloud home'.

q: Who invented the telephone?
explanation:
Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876. Chadwick discovered the neutron (1932), and Pasteur developed pasteurisation and the rabies vaccine.
Memory hook: telephone BELL rings.

q: Who is the real founder of Microsoft?
options: Bill Gates and Paul G. Allen
explanation:
Microsoft was founded in 1975 in Albuquerque by childhood friends Bill Gates and Paul Allen. Systrom and Krieger founded Instagram, and Zuckerberg founded Facebook.
Memory hook: Gates + Allen = MS (Micro-Soft).

q: What is the colour of polar bear's skin?
explanation:
A polar bear's skin is black, which absorbs heat. Its fur is actually transparent, hollow hair that looks white by scattering light.
Memory hook: white coat, black skin - dressed for the Arctic.

q: Which of the following is a common cause for the rise of dictatorship?
explanation:
Economic crises (depression, unemployment, inflation) breed discontent that dictators exploit, e.g. Hitler after the Great Depression and the Weimar hyperinflation. The other options strengthen democracy.
Memory hook: empty stomachs -> strongmen.

q: Which of the following prevents wastage of water?
explanation:
Sprinkler (and drip) irrigation sprays water like rain only where it is needed. This cuts seepage and evaporation losses compared with flood/canal irrigation. Canals, wells and tube wells are water sources, not water-saving methods.
Memory hook: sprinkle, don't flood.

q: Name the instrument that is used to measure blood pressure.
explanation:
A sphygmomanometer (BP cuff) measures blood pressure in mmHg. A glucometer measures blood sugar, and a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.
Memory hook: sphygmos = pulse (Greek) -> pulse-pressure meter.

q: What is India's national sport?
explanation:
Field hockey is popularly regarded as India's national game because of India's 8 Olympic hockey gold medals (6 in a row from 1928 to 1956).
Memory hook: 8 Olympic golds -> hockey.
note: Officially, the Government of India has not declared any national sport (Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports RTI reply, 2012). Hockey is the conventional exam answer.

q: In which of the following years was the Environment Protection Act enacted?
explanation:
The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was enacted after the Bhopal gas tragedy (December 1984). It is an 'umbrella' law implementing the Stockholm Conference (1972) decisions.
Memory hook: Bhopal '84 -> EPA '86.

q: Which State is known as the 'spice garden of India'?
explanation:
Kerala is called the 'Spice Garden of India' because of its pepper, cardamom, clove, cinnamon and nutmeg. Pepper from the Malabar coast drew Arab and European traders.
Memory hook: Vasco da Gama sailed to Kerala (Calicut) for spices.

q: Who was the second Chief Minister of Meghalaya?
explanation:
Captain Williamson A. Sangma was the first CM (1972-1978). Darwin Diengdoh Pugh (HSPDP) became the second CM in March 1978. B.B. Lyngdoh and P.A. Sangma came later.
Memory hook: W then D - Williamson first, Darwin (Diengdoh Pugh) second.

q: Three candidates contested an election and received 1136, 7636 and 11628 votes respectively. What percentage of the total votes did the winning candidate get?
A person crosses a 600 m long street in 5 minutes. What is his speed in km/hr?
explanation:
Speed $=\frac{600\text{ m}}{5\text{ min}}=120$ m/min
In km/hr: $120\times60=7200$ m/hr $=7.2$ km/hr

q: A train running at the speed of 60 km/hr crosses a pole in 9 seconds. What is the length of the train?
explanation:
Speed $=60\times\frac{5}{18}=\frac{50}{3}$ m/s
Crossing a pole: length = speed $\times$ time
Length $=\frac{50}{3}\times9=150$ m

q: A sum of money at simple interest amounts to ₹815 in 3 years and ₹854 in 4 years. The sum of money is
explanation:
SI for 1 year $=854-815=39$
SI for 3 years $=3\times39=117$
Principal $=815-117=698$, i.e. Rs. 698

q: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 5 hours and 6 hours respectively. Pipe C can empty it in 12 hours. If all the three pipes are opened together, then the tank will be filled in
explanation:
Net rate $=\frac15+\frac16-\frac1{12}=\frac{12+10-5}{60}=\frac{17}{60}$ tank/hr
Time $=\frac{60}{17}=3\frac{9}{17}$ hours

q: The sum of the two numbers is 12 and their product is 35. What is the sum of the reciprocals of these numbers?
explanation:
$\frac1x+\frac1y=\frac{x+y}{xy}$
$=\frac{12}{35}$
(Check: the numbers are 5 and 7; $\frac15+\frac17=\frac{12}{35}$)

q: The average weight of A, B and C is 45 kg. If the average weight of A and B is 40 kg and that of B and C is 43 kg, then the weight of B is
The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 60 years. Six years ago, father's age was five times the age of the son. After 6 years, son's age will be
explanation:
Let son $=s$, father $=60-s$
Six years ago: $60-s-6=5(s-6)$
$54-s=5s-30\Rightarrow6s=84\Rightarrow s=14$
After 6 years: $14+6=20$ years

q: Which one of the following is not a prime number?
explanation:
$91=7\times13$, so it is composite.
31, 61 and 71 have no factor up to their square roots (primes 2, 3, 5, 7), so they are prime.
Hook: 91 looks prime but is $7\times13$.

q: Complete the following series : FAG, GAF, HAI, IAH, ____
explanation:
First letters: F, G, H, I, J (+1 each).
Middle letter is always A.
Pairs: FAG then GAF (first and last swapped); HAI then IAH (swapped).
Next pair starts after I, H: J _ K pattern: first letter J, last letter K (F-G, H-I, J-K).
Answer: JAK

q: Two numbers are respectively 20% and 50% more than a third number. The ratio of the two numbers is
explanation:
Let the third number be 100.
First $=120$, second $=150$
Ratio $=120:150=4:5$

q: A and B can do a work in 8 days, B and C can do the same work in 12 days. A, B and C together can finish it in 6 days. A and C together will do it in
explanation:
Rates: $A+B=\frac18$, $B+C=\frac1{12}$, $A+B+C=\frac16$
$B=\frac18+\frac1{12}-\frac16=\frac{3+2-4}{24}=\frac1{24}$
$A+C=\frac16-\frac1{24}=\frac{3}{24}=\frac18$
A and C together take 8 days

q: The LCM of two numbers is 48. The numbers are in the ratio 2 : 3. Then the sum of the numbers is
explanation:
Numbers $=2k,3k$; LCM $=6k=48\Rightarrow k=8$
Numbers: 16 and 24
Sum $=40$

q: Which of the following is equal to $3.14\times10^6$?
explanation:
$10^6$ moves the decimal point 6 places right.
$3.14\times10^6=3140000$

A man buys a cycle for ₹1,400 and sells it at a loss of 15%. What is the selling price of the cycle?
The average age of 5 men is 40. The average age of 5 women is 39. The average age of their 4 children is 15. What is the average age of a family?
explanation:
Total age of men $=5\times40=200$
Total age of women $=5\times39=195$
Total age of children $=4\times15=60$
Total $=455$ for $5+5+4=14$ people
Average $=\frac{455}{14}=32.5$
32.5 is not among the options (closest printed option is 30.33).
note: Official key: full marks to all (NOTA). Correct value is 32.5 (455/14), which is not among the options. answer index set to the closest option (30.33) only as a placeholder.

q: A man travelled 30% of his journey at a speed of 85 km/hr and the rest of his journey at a speed of 33 km/hr. Find his average speed throughout the journey.
explanation:
Let total distance $=100$ km
Time for 30 km at 85 km/hr $=\frac{30}{85}=0.3529$ hr
Time for 70 km at 33 km/hr $=\frac{70}{33}=2.1212$ hr
Total time $=2.4742$ hr
Average speed $=\frac{100}{2.4742}\approx40.42$ km/hr
40.42 is not among the options (closest printed option is 42.6).
note: Official key: full marks to all (NOTA). Correct value is about 40.42 km/hr, which is not among the options. answer index set to the closest option (42.6) only as a placeholder. A stray mark above the '3' in '33' is a print artefact.

q: 15 men can do a work in 25 days. Find the time in which 20 men can do the same amount of work.
explanation:
Total work $=15\times25=375$ man-days
Time for 20 men $=\frac{375}{20}=18.75$ days
This rounds up to 19 days (the official answer); no option is exactly 18.75.
note: Exact answer is 18.75 days, which is not printed. The official key gives (B) 19 days, presumably 18.75 rounded up to whole days.

q: The ratio between the perimeter and the breadth of a rectangle is 5 : 1. If the area of the rectangle is 216 sq. cm, what is the length of the rectangle?
explanation:
$2(l+b)=5b\Rightarrow2l=3b\Rightarrow l=1.5b$
Area $=1.5b^2=216\Rightarrow b^2=144\Rightarrow b=12$
$l=1.5\times12=18$ cm

q: Find the value of the blank place : $\sqrt{0.0169}\times\underline{\ ?\ }=1.3$
note: The printed radical has no bar over the '? ', so it covers only 0.0169; that reading gives the official answer 10.

q: Find the value of $(1000)^9\div10^{24}$.
If 25% of a number is 25 less than the number, find the number.
A train moving at a speed of 58 km/hr passes a pole in 7.4 seconds. Find the length of the train.
explanation:
Speed $=58\times\frac5{18}=16.11$ m/s
Length $=16.11\times7.4\approx119.2$ m

q: What will be the circumference of the circle if its area is numerically equal to twice its circumference?
explanation:
$\pi r^2=2\times2\pi r\Rightarrow r=4$
Circumference $=2\pi r=8\pi\approx25.14$ (with $\pi\approx3.1428$)

q: The cost price of an article is 80% of its selling price. Find the profit percentage.
explanation:
Let SP $=100$, then CP $=80$
Profit $=20$
Profit % $=\frac{20}{80}\times100=25\%$

q: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 15 and 1560. If one of the numbers is 120, find the other.
explanation:
Product of the numbers = HCF $\times$ LCM
Other $=\frac{15\times1560}{120}=195$

q: If $x+y=21$ and $xy=110$, find the value of $x^2+y^2$.
The ratio of two numbers is 11 : 12. If the sum of the numbers is 253, find the difference between the numbers.
explanation:
$11k+12k=253\Rightarrow k=11$
Numbers: 121 and 132
Difference $=k=11$

q: Five cubes each of side 6 cm are joined end-to-end. What will be the volume (in cubic cm) of the cuboid so formed?
explanation:
Volume is unchanged by joining: $5\times6^3=5\times216=1080$ cm$^3$
(Cuboid $30\times6\times6=1080$)

q: 2 pipes can fill a tank in 12 minutes when opened together. If first pipe can fill the tank in 16 minutes, find the time taken by the second pipe to fill the tank.
explanation:
Second pipe rate $=\frac1{12}-\frac1{16}=\frac{4-3}{48}=\frac1{48}$
Time $=48$ minutes

q: The speed of a train is 45 km/hr. Find the time required by the train to cross a station of 500 m if the train is 340 m long.
explanation:
Distance $=500+340=840$ m
Speed $=45\times\frac5{18}=12.5$ m/s
Time $=\frac{840}{12.5}=67.2$ s $=1.12$ minutes

q: Consider the following series : 7, 10, 8, 11, 9, 12, ... What number should come next in the above series?
explanation:
Pattern alternates $+3,-2$: $7\to10\to8\to11\to9\to12$
Next: $12-2=10$

q: What will be the area of a square (in cm$^2$) that can be inscribed in a circle of radius 6 cm?
explanation:
Diagonal of the square = diameter $=12$ cm
Area $=\frac{d^2}{2}=\frac{144}{2}=72$ cm$^2$

q: A group of 5 men or 12 women can do a task in 78 days. Find the time taken by 5 men and 12 women to complete the task.
explanation:
5 men = 12 women (same work in same time)
5 men + 12 women = two such groups, so they work twice as fast
Time $=\frac{78}{2}=39$ days

q: If the side of a cube is increased to two times, then the surface will become how many times?
explanation:
Surface area $=6a^2$
With side $2a$: $6(2a)^2=24a^2=4\times6a^2$
Surface becomes 4 times (volume would be 8 times)

q: How many prime numbers are less than 70?
Find the value of $\sqrt{2+\left(\frac{41}{64}\right)}$.
The ratio between two numbers is 2 : 11. If the difference between the numbers is 81, find the smaller number.
explanation:
$11k-2k=9k=81\Rightarrow k=9$
Smaller number $=2\times9=18$

q: If the salaries of two people a and b are increased by 40% and 50% respectively and the final salary after the promotion is same, find the ratio of their initial salaries.
How much time will it take for an amount of ₹450 to yield ₹81 as interest at 4.5% per annum of simple interest?
explanation:
$T=\frac{SI\times100}{P\times R}$
$=\frac{81\times100}{450\times4.5}=\frac{8100}{2025}=4$ years

q: What percentage of numbers from 1 to 70 has 1 or 9 in the unit's digit?
explanation:
Each block of 10 has two such numbers (ending in 1 and 9)
From 1 to 70: $7\times2=14$ numbers
Percentage $=\frac{14}{70}\times100=20\%$

q: Find the number of triangles in the given figure : [Figure: a trapezium with a rectangle inside it (two vertical lines from the top corners to the base). A diagonal runs from the top-left corner of the rectangle to its bottom-right corner; one slanting line runs from the bottom-left corner of the rectangle up to a point on the top edge, and another from a point on the base up to the top-right corner.]
explanation:
Count systematically by lines. Lines: base, top, two outer slant sides, two verticals, the long diagonal, and two inner slants.
Every set of 3 lines that meet pairwise at 3 distinct points on the drawn segments gives one triangle.
Counting all such sets (checked by computer on the figure) gives 14.
Tip: label every intersection point and count triangles with each point as the top vertex to avoid double counting.
note: Figure described in words; count verified by enumerating line triples on a coordinate model of the printed figure.

q: The profit made by selling an article for 720 is 20%. Find the cost price.
Find the sum of $9+\frac{1}{\sqrt9}+\frac{1}{9+\sqrt9}-\frac{1}{9-\sqrt9}$
Find the least square number which is divisible by 24, 25, 30 and 36.
explanation:
LCM$(24,25,30,36)=2^3\times3^2\times5^2=1800$
To make it a perfect square, the exponent of 2 must be even: multiply by 2
Least square $=3600$

q: The average age of 5 boys of a class is 15. If 7 more boys are admitted to the class with average age 12 and 3 of the existing boys leave the class with the average age 13, what will be the new average age of the boys of the class?
explanation:
Initial total $=5\times15=75$
Add 7 boys: $+7\times12=84$
Remove 3 boys: $-3\times13=39$
New total $=75+84-39=120$ for $5+7-3=9$ boys
Average $=\frac{120}{9}\approx13.3$

q: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 33 and 4719 respectively. When the first number is divided by 3, the quotient is 121. Find the other number.
explanation:
First number $=3\times121=363$
Other $=\frac{33\times4719}{363}=429$

q: A number is selected at random from the first fifty natural numbers. What is the probability that the number is divisible by 2, 3 and 4?
explanation:
Divisible by 2, 3 and 4 means divisible by LCM $=12$
Multiples of 12 up to 50: 12, 24, 36, 48 (4 numbers)
$P=\frac{4}{50}=\frac{2}{25}$

q: Find the ten's digit in the expression $65^2-55^2$.
